jobs.description:
What will you do?

A day in the life of the Environmental and Social Responsibility (E&SR) Reporting and Compliance Project Coordinator at VF looks a little like this.

The E&SR Reporting and Compliance Project Coordinator will support VF Corporation’s E&SR reporting initiatives through project support, tracking and monitoring global regulations and reporting requirements, internal compliance support, and research and analysis.

As part of VF’s E&SR Reporting team, the E&SR Reporting and Compliance Project Coordinator will have the unique opportunity to collaborate with teams across the global enterprise including, but not limited to, sustainability, legal, finance, product stewardship, responsible sourcing, inclusion and diversity, government affairs, communications and supply chain.

Let’s break down that day-in-the-life a bit more.

Reporting support:

Implement project management best practices for cross-functional Environmental and Social Responsibility reporting initiatives.
Provide ongoing project management support, including developing project timelines, coordinating meetings and stakeholder outreach, and regularly updating reporting management systems.
Support the development of regulatory and voluntary disclosures, including CSRD, ISSB, CDP, stakeholder questionnaires, ESG ratings, ad hoc requests, and website updates.
Support the content and data collection and review process.
Monitor current and emerging ESG regulatory requirements.
Regularly update internal stakeholders on evolving ESG regulatory timelines and requirements.
Conduct research, analysis, and benchmarking on key sustainability topics, gaps and opportunities, and peer disclosures.

What do you need to succeed?

We all have unique skills that we bring to work and celebrate every day. For this role, there are foundation skills you’ll need to succeed and excel. Additionally, while formal education in a related field is great to have, we are most interested in your 1 + years of experience and professional achievements.

The foundation skills you will need in this position are:

Educational Requirements: Bachelor's degree in related field required. Master’s degree preferred.
Demonstrated familiarity with ESG reporting and regulatory frameworks, including CSRD, ISSB, and TCFD, and the broader regulatory landscape.
Experience collecting ESG-related data, including environmental and social data sets.
Proficiency using Excel, Smartsheet, or similar tools to support analysis and reporting.
Exceptional attention to detail and ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present information succinctly and visually to a variety of stakeholders.
Experience working cross-functionally and tailoring communications for different stakeholders.
Ability to support multiple projects and cross-functional teams.
Self-motivated and able to work independently with limited supervision.
Ability to prioritize and manage workload based on deadlines and resource availability.
Location requirement: hybrid role in Denver, CO.

in the Mid-Atlantic
region. This position offers the flexibility to be located in our Fairfax, Richmond, or Virginia Beach, Virginia

Whether you’re an experienced professional or a new graduate, you’ll have the chance to collaborate with the best and brightest and work on innovative and complex projects at the forefront of the industry. Must be willing/able to perform field work
Lead field delineations of Waters of the U.S., including wetlands, and conduct stream assessments
Coordinate site visits with clients and regulatory agencies in the field
Prepare delineation reports, functional assessments, Jurisdictional Determinations (JD) requests, Perennial Flow Determinations (PFD), and Water Quality Impact Assessments (WQIA)
Lead multi-faceted projects in collaboration with scientists, engineers, and subconsultants
Prepare Clean Water Act (CWA) 404/401 permit applications
Prepare CWA 402 Registration Statements and Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans (SWPPP)

Assist team members with fieldwork, technical reports, technical reports, agency coordination, and quality control
Assist with the preparation of proposals/pursuits, provide technical input, and contribute to proposal writing

5+ years of applicable experience, including project/task management experience
B.S. in Environmental Science, Biology, Ecology, Environmental Studies, Forestry, Wildlife Biology, Geology, or a related field
Professional Wetland Delineator (PWD), Professional Wetland Scientist (PWS), Virginia State Waters Delineator (VSWD), ISA Certified Arborist, or similar certification is preferred
Proficiency with ArcGIS PRO, AutoCAD, and/or MicroStation is preferred
Ability to lead environmental permitting and NEPA processes and coordinate with clients and regulatory agencies
Experience preparing and submitting Clean Water Act 404/401 permit applications and NEPA documentation
Experience coordinating with state, federal, and local regulatory agencies
Knowledge of state (Virginia) and federal legislation as it relates to CWA Sections 401/404 permitting and NEPA
Knowledge and understanding of complex regulatory issues and regulatory changes

Ability to manage multiple projects

This position is based on Stanford’s main campus with consideration given to the option for a hybrid work schedule (partially onsite 3 or more days a week), subject to operational need.

Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa.

About Us

The Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability strives to create a future when humans and nature thrive in concert and in perpetuity. The school is made up of a three-part structure to drive global impact: Our academic departments and programs educate students and create new knowledge across areas of research that are crucial for advancing the long-term prosperity of the planet and people; Institutes bridge scholarship at Stanford and beyond, bringing multiple viewpoints to bear on urgent challenges; The Sustainability Accelerator drives new policy and technology solutions through a worldwide network of partners who work with our teams to develop solutions at a global scale. The school is dedicated to creating and supporting a community with the richness of experience and background needed to create solutions that benefit all people, particularly those most affected by environmental damage and climate change.

For more information on the school, click here .

The SDSS Sustainability Accelerator (the Sustainability Accelerator) serves as a launchpad for sustainability solutions, turning innovative ideas into transformative and scalable technologies and policies that will substantially improve the quality of human life and our planet. The Sustainability Accelerator is rooted in the Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability and works across the University and with external partners to drive solutions from the lab into the world.

The Accelerator is seeking a full-time Administrative Associate to join our operations team and provide administrative and programmatic support across our growing portfolio of sustainability initiatives. This position will serve as the primary administrative contact for four portfolios of faculty research projects (“Flagships”) managed by the Accelerator, supporting their day-to-day coordination and helping connect faculty, research teams, and Accelerator staff with the administrative resources they need. We are looking for a highly organized, collaborative, and service-oriented professional who brings strong communication skills, careful attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple priorities.
